author: bryclevgp
title: Keep Get answers in the thread, size the follow-up, report back once per priority
body:
Why: the follow-up text, Get answers and report back each let the official lose the thread or get told something untrue.

- The follow-up reads Draft until its recipients are picked, then Scheduled, never In review. Its undrawn list stays off Constituents lists and is locked against edit and delete by direct link. It is sized to at most 90% of the people left after the first half, so a few opt-outs before the draw still leave it full. The drew-nobody cancel stays, with its refund line.
- Get answers shows only once a check is out and the read is short. Before that the strip and rail say "No one asked yet". While a follow-up is scheduled the button gives way to "Follow-up text to N people on date". The agent treats it as a detour: it proposes text, calls and doors aimed at the missing groups, never a third text, never starts the civic panel, and returns to the step in one line. gp-api refuses a text card while a follow-up is scheduled or sent, and validates `roundTwoSize` against the split `size_round_one` makes. The most and least affected follow-up path is gone from the priority prompt, and the dead `panelSampleSize` path with it.
- Report back is one card per priority, to everyone who answered on any channel, counted once. A new card shows each time the read status changes and says where the read stands and what to do. A second report back is allowed once the read changes.
- The Chief of Staff "What's a civic panel?" explainer now ends on "Grow your civic panel" for offices with members.

Not touched: the lower-level `panelSize` list sample in contacts/contracts, which nothing in the product sends now. Pre-existing local failures outside this diff: geoapify vendor-mock routes (gp-api) and DoorKnockingPack schema messages (contracts).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Medium Risk**
> Changes checkout sizing, report-back audience, purchase deduplication, and Chief of Staff gating for civic-panel priorities—high user impact but covered by broad test updates.
> 
> **Overview**
> Aligns civic-panel priority flows so officials see accurate status, follow-ups size safely, Get answers stays in-thread, and report-back targets everyone who answered—not just one text send.
> 
> **Follow-up text:** Checkout caps the held half at **90%** of people left after round one (`FOLLOW_UP_POOL_SHARE`). Contracts and `PriorityReadStatus` add **`checkOut`**, **`followUpSent`**, and stricter follow-up UI copy. The agent and **`checkFollowUpPart`** block another text while a follow-up is scheduled or after it sent (doors/calls only; no third text); **`roundTwoSize`** must match **`size_round_one`**. **`panelSampleSize`** is removed from outreach proposals and related validation.
> 
> **Get answers:** Prompt/handler changes treat it as a **detour** that proposes outreach to underrepresented groups and returns to the active step; no civic-panel setup from the priority thread. “Most/least affected” post-round-one path is removed in favor of groups the read names.
> 
> **Report back:** Audience is **everyone who answered the priority once** across text, calls, and doors (`answeredPersonIds`); list samples and `drawListSample` use that set. Dashboard cards are **one per priority**, keyed by **read status** (new card when status changes); checkout/claim dedupes per priority since the latest card. `OutreachReportBackService` and purchase validation follow the new rules.
> 
> Docs/product copy (`civic-panel-mrp`, `productMap`, AGENTS) updated to match; tests expanded across round-two, report-back, dashboard cards, and priority read-status.
> 
> <sup>Reviewed by [Cursor Bugbot](https://cursor.com/bugbot) for commit 278ea8bcf8002c500f6e2d84d6a7ebf73a3e29ab. Configure [here](https://www.cursor.com/dashboard/bugbot).</sup>
<!-- /CURSOR_SUMMARY -->

diff --git a/packages/gp-api/src/chats/CLIENT_HOOKUP.md b/packages/gp-api/src/chats/CLIENT_HOOKUP.md
index a45ab3ac..64ace5a6 100644

@@ -52,32 +52,32 @@ Request body:
 }
 ```
 
-| Field | Required | Notes |
-|---|---|---|
-| `content` | yes | Trimmed; max 10,000 chars; empty rejected with 400 |
+| Field             | Required | Notes                                                             |
+| ----------------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `content`         | yes      | Trimmed; max 10,000 chars; empty rejected with 400                |
 | `clientMessageId` | optional | UUID v4. **Strongly recommended** — see idempotency section below |
 
 Response is **SSE** (`Content-Type: text/event-stream`). Each frame is `data: <JSON>\n\n`. The JSON shape is one of:
 
-| Type | Fields | Meaning |
-|---|---|---|
-| `text` | `{ type: 'text', delta: string }` | Token-by-token assistant output. Append to a buffer. |
-| `tool_call` | `{ type: 'tool_call', toolName: string, args: object }` | The LLM invoked a tool. Show "thinking" / "searching" UI if you want. |
-| `tool_result` | `{ type: 'tool_result', toolName: string, result: object }` | Tool finished. |
-| `done` | `{ type: 'done', assistantMessageId?: string }` | Stream complete. `assistantMessageId` may be omitted if persistence failed; don't depend on it being present. |
-| `error` | `{ type: 'error', code, message, retryable }` | Stream failed. See error codes below. |
+| Type          | Fields                                                      | Meaning                                                                                                       |
+| ------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `text`        | `{ type: 'text', delta: string }`                           | Token-by-token assistant output. Append to a buffer.                                                          |
+| `tool_call`   | `{ type: 'tool_call', toolName: string, args: object }`     | The LLM invoked a tool. Show "thinking" / "searching" UI if you want.                                         |
+| `tool_result` | `{ type: 'tool_result', toolName: string, result: object }` | Tool finished.                                                                                                |
+| `done`        | `{ type: 'done', assistantMessageId?: string }`             | Stream complete. `assistantMessageId` may be omitted if persistence failed; don't depend on it being present. |
+| `error`       | `{ type: 'error', code, message, retryable }`               | Stream failed. See error codes below.                                                                         |
 
 Always handle `done` and `error` as terminal — close the stream and stop reading.
 
 ### Error codes
 
-| `code` | `retryable` | When | Suggested UI |
-|---|---|---|---|
-| `conversation_not_found` | false | Annotation isn't a chat / chatConversationId is null / wrong owner | "This chat is unavailable. Refresh the briefing." |
-| `upstream_unavailable` | true | LLM provider 5xx / network failure | "Chat is temporarily unavailable. Retry?" + retry button |
-| `rate_limited` | true | LLM provider 429 | "Too many requests. Try again in a moment." + retry |
-| `aborted` | false | Client closed connection or server cancelled | Show nothing (user did it themselves). |
-| `internal` | false | Anything else server-side | "Something went wrong. Please refresh." |
+| `code`                   | `retryable` | When                                                               | Suggested UI                                             |
+| ------------------------ | ----------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------ | -------------------------------------------------------- |
+| `conversation_not_found` | false       | Annotation isn't a chat / chatConversationId is null / wrong owner | "This chat is unavailable. Refresh the briefing."        |
+| `upstream_unavailable`   | true        | LLM provider 5xx / network failure                                 | "Chat is temporarily unavailable. Retry?" + retry button |
+| `rate_limited`           | true        | LLM provider 429                                                   | "Too many requests. Try again in a moment." + retry      |
+| `aborted`                | false       | Client closed connection or server cancelled                       | Show nothing (user did it themselves).                   |
+| `internal`               | false       | Anything else server-side                                          | "Something went wrong. Please refresh."                  |
 
 Always show `message` to the user — it's already sanitized server-side (no stack traces, no internal model names, no provider URLs).
 
@@ -102,6 +102,7 @@ async function send(content: string) {
 ```
 
 What this prevents:
+
 - **Double-click on Send** — two POSTs with the same `clientMessageId` → only one user message persisted, only one LLM stream runs. (Best UX is still to disable the Send button while the request is in flight; idempotency is a backstop.)
 - **Network-retry mid-send** — client times out, retries → same id → backend returns the existing message instead of running the LLM twice.

 {
   "conversationId": "ckg...",

-    "byModel": [{ "model": "claude-sonnet-4-6", "inputTokens": 1200, "outputTokens": 340 }]

 }
 ```
@@ -145,10 +153,10 @@ Thumbs up / thumbs down on one assistant reply, plus the optional note explainin
 { "feedback": "negative", "comment": "Missed the budget item." }
 ```
 
-| Field | Required | Notes |
-|---|---|---|
-| `feedback` | yes | `positive` \| `negative` |
-| `comment` | optional | Max 2,000 chars. **Omit** it to keep whatever note is stored (a re-vote without retyping); pass `null` to clear it |

 `PUT` is an upsert, so repeating it replaces the rating rather than stacking rows, and it returns the stored row. `DELETE` retracts the rating and its note (204, and idempotent — retracting nothing still succeeds).
 
@@ -157,6 +165,7 @@ Both 404 on a `messageId` that isn't an **assistant** turn of that conversation,
 ## DELETE `:annotationId` — soft-delete
 
 Returns 204 No Content. Soft-deletes the underlying `ChatConversation` (sets `deletedAt`). After deletion:
+
 - `GET` returns 404
 - `POST` returns `conversation_not_found` over SSE

 const messageId = crypto.randomUUID()
 const controller = new AbortController()

-)
+const res = await fetch(`/api/v1/briefing-chats/${annotationId}/messages`, {
+  method: 'POST',
+  headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json' },
+  body: JSON.stringify({ content, clientMessageId: messageId }),
+  signal: controller.signal,
+})
 
 if (!res.ok) {
   // 4xx/5xx before stream starts — read JSON body for error
@@ -203,11 +209,21 @@ while (true) {
     if (!frame.startsWith('data: ')) continue
     const chunk = JSON.parse(frame.slice(6))
     switch (chunk.type) {
-      case 'text': assistantText += chunk.delta; renderPartial(assistantText); break
-      case 'tool_call': renderToolThinking(chunk.toolName); break
-      case 'tool_result': /* optional, usually ignored in UI */ break
-      case 'done': finalize(assistantText, chunk.assistantMessageId); return
-      case 'error': showError(chunk); return
+      case 'text':
+        assistantText += chunk.delta
+        renderPartial(assistantText)
+        break
+      case 'tool_call':
+        renderToolThinking(chunk.toolName)
+        break
+      case 'tool_result':
+        /* optional, usually ignored in UI */ break
+      case 'done':
+        finalize(assistantText, chunk.assistantMessageId)
+        return
+      case 'error':
+        showError(chunk)
+        return
     }
   }
 }

Exactly ONE refund per charge: the refund is claimed to the in-flight `refunding` state (single-owner CAS) BEFORE the Stripe call and keyed on the durable charge id (`p2p-sms-refund-<chargeId>`), so a deny and a cancel racing the same charge can neither both claim it nor both pass the key; a transient refund failure reverts `refunding → captured` to retry. A caller that OBSERVES another owner's `refunding` never assumes success: it polls until the row resolves — `refunded` → report it, reverted to `captured` → re-attempt (claim the CAS itself), still `refunding` past the bound (owner crashed between claim and Stripe) → surface UNRESOLVED (`ServiceUnavailable`) WITHOUT reporting a refund or flipping the spine, so a candidate is never told "refunded" unless the refund committed (the stranded row is a slice-F reconcile case). A `capturing` row is REFUSED (money mid-flight). A row a promotion code settled at $0 (`captured`, `capturedAmountInCents: 0`) or covered before capture (`authorized`, no intent) has nothing to void or refund: it is released to `voided` with no Stripe call and the free-texts offer handed back. Stripe has already counted the code's redemption; a release does not reactivate it. A refund of a promo send refunds the charge, which returns only what was captured. The refund resolves off the satellite intent (`chargeIntentId`, falling back to the live PI's charge for a stale authorized→succeeded row), never the checkout session, and a refund Stripe accepts but does not process (status not `succeeded`/`pending`) is reverted, never reported refunded. `cancel` posts the CAS "canceled" Slack notice (best-effort), parity with the shared immediate-charge body. A row the live paths deliberately leave non-terminal (stranded `refunding`, denied-but-unreleased, or a failed best-effort void/restore) is healed by `outreachP2pSmsReconcile.service.ts` below A serial-only account-wide voice-call COUNT speedup (`source: 'count'`) is the documented extension point behind the seam but is DEFERRED (`credits_usage` was account-wide + omitted `start_date` + unverified), so the system is correct-but-slower on the floor alone. The deadlock backstop's timer is the STABLE `dialingStartedAt` (stamped at the dial claim, never bumped by recovery's self-transition, which bumps `@updatedAt`). `ROBOCALL_SEND_MAX_PER_SWEEP=0` is kept as the kill-switch (pauses every launch, no deploy), capped at one per pass by the gate; `ROBOCALL_SEND_LAUNCH_SPACING_MS` + the `over_cps_limit` BREAK are a defensive multi-launch net (`startCampaign`'s throttle revert is the real self-correction if the gate ever lets two overlap). `CALLHUB_VB_CALLS_PER_MINUTE` (default 120 as of 2026-10-15; see "Frequency" below) is the per-campaign dial rate. READS the hold only — no capture/void, no completion poll. The commit (`commitDialed`, reached from the happy launch AND from `reconcileDialing`'s STARTED resolution) also best-effort advances the spine `Outreach.status pending → in_progress` (CAS-guarded on `pending`, idempotent, never flips a canceled/failed row) so the history UI shows "Sending" during the run window. It writes NO per-contact `ContactInteractionRobocall` rows — this billing model does not know who was reached, so only the aggregate count lives on the `OutreachRobocall` row. --- /dev/null
+++ b/packages/gp-api/src/priorities/util/priorityRespondents.util.ts
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+import {
+  OutreachStatus,
+  OutreachType,
+  PollIndividualMessageSender,
+  type PrismaClient,
+} from '../../generated/prisma'
+
+type RespondentsClient = Pick<
+  PrismaClient,
+  | 'outreach'
+  | 'pollIndividualMessage'
+  | 'contactInteractionText'
+  | 'contactInteractionPhoneBanking'
+  | 'contactInteractionDoorKnock'
+>
+
+// A priority's sends are the ones past checkout.
+export const PRIORITY_UNSENT_STATUSES: OutreachStatus[] = [
+  OutreachStatus.pending_payment,
+  OutreachStatus.draft,
+  OutreachStatus.canceled,
+]
+
+// Who has answered a priority on any channel, each person once: a text
+// reply that was more than STOP, an answered call or an answered door.
+// Someone heard by text and at the door is one person. People who have
+// opted out of the office's texts are left out, since this is who the
+// priority's report back goes to.
+export const answeredPersonIds = async (
+  client: RespondentsClient,
+  organizationSlug: string,
+  priorityId: string,
+): Promise<string[]> => {
+  const sends = await client.outreach.findMany({
+    where: {
+      priorityId,
+      organizationSlug,
+      campaignId: null,
+      status: { notIn: PRIORITY_UNSENT_STATUSES },
+      outreachType: {
+        in: [
+          OutreachType.text,
+          OutreachType.nativePhoneBanking,
+          OutreachType.nativeDoorKnocking,
+        ],
+      },
+    },
+    select: { id: true, outreachType: true, phoneBankingListId: true },
+  })
+  const idsOf = (type: OutreachType): number[] =>
+    sends.filter((send) => send.outreachType === type).map((send) => send.id)
+  const phoneBankingListIds = sends.flatMap((send) =>
+    send.outreachType === OutreachType.nativePhoneBanking &&
+    send.phoneBankingListId !== null
+      ? [send.phoneBankingListId]
+      : [],
+  )
+  const [texts, calls, doors] = await Promise.all([
+    client.pollIndividualMessage.findMany({
+      where: {
+        outreachId: { in: idsOf(OutreachType.text) },
+        sender: PollIndividualMessageSender.CONSTITUENT,
+        NOT: { isOptOut: true },
+      },
+      select: { personId: true },
+      distinct: ['personId'],
+    }),
+    client.contactInteractionPhoneBanking.findMany({
+      where: {
+        phoneBankingListId: { in: phoneBankingListIds },
+        outcome: 'answered',
+      },
+      select: { personId: true },
+      distinct: ['personId'],
+    }),
+    client.contactInteractionDoorKnock.findMany({
+      where: {
+        organizationSlug,
+        outreachId: { in: idsOf(OutreachType.nativeDoorKnocking) },
+        outcome: 'answered',
+      },
+      select: { personId: true },
+      distinct: ['personId'],
+    }),
+  ])
+  const answered = [
+    ...new Set([...texts, ...calls, ...doors].map(({ personId }) => personId)),
+  ]
+  if (answered.length === 0) return []
+  const optedOut = await client.contactInteractionText.findMany({
+    where: {
+      organizationSlug,
+      personId: { in: answered },
+      optedOutAt: { not: null },
+    },
+    select: { personId: true },
+    distinct: ['personId'],
+  })
+  const out = new Set(optedOut.map(({ personId }) => personId))
+  return answered.filter((personId) => !out.has(personId))
+}

priorFindings.body:
`followUpsFor` queries follow-up rows with `status: { notIn: UNSENT_STATUSES }` where `UNSENT_STATUSES` now includes `denied` and `failed`. This means a denied or failed follow-up is excluded from the query entirely — no map entry is created for that priority. `outreachState` therefore emits neither `followUp` nor `followUpSent`, and `canGetAnswers` in `readStatusCopy.ts` (line 28-32) sees `!read.followUpSent === true` and shows the **Get answers** button even though the follow-up was denied or failed.

The intent of adding `denied`/`failed` to `PRIORITY_UNSENT_STATUSES` was to fix this gap, but the fix over-corrects: instead of treating those statuses as terminal (like `in_progress`/`completed`), it hides them from the query entirely — producing the same UI bug as before.

The fix is to keep `denied`/`failed` out of `UNSENT_STATUSES` so they appear in the query results, and handle them in the loop as terminal states that set `state.sent = true`.

**Falsification check:** No other field in `PriorityReadStatus` signals a denied/failed follow-up, and no upstream guard suppresses `canGetAnswers` for this case — confirmed by reading `outreachState`, `canGetAnswers`, and the full `followUpsFor` query.
